title: JavaScript Developer Tools

content.intro: This lesson introduces JavaScript Developer Tools using the supplied syllabus terms, a visual map, and a short inspectable example.
content.why_it_matters: Understanding JavaScript Developer Tools helps you make JavaScript behavior explicit instead of relying on guesswork. The skill becomes more valuable as programs combine data, user input, runtime APIs, and failures.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: JavaScript Developer Tools is one of the named concepts in the JavaScript syllabus. Focus on the behavior it defines, the inputs that influence that behavior, and the result you can observe. JavaScript language semantics are specified by ECMAScript; browser and Node.js APIs belong to their host runtimes, so check which environment a feature requires.

content_blocks.title: Guided example
content_blocks.text: First, name the expected result for JavaScript Developer Tools. Then trace the code one statement at a time: record the important value before and after each operation, and check whether the output matches your expectation. Change one input or condition; if the result is different, inspect that step instead of rewriting the whole program.

content_blocks.title: Environment and correctness note
content_blocks.text: The ECMAScript 2026 edition is the stable language reference used by this course. The browser DOM, Fetch API, and Node.js APIs are host features. Emerging proposals and runtime support can change; verify compatibility before depending on a feature in production.

content.task: Try it yourself: create a small program that demonstrates JavaScript Developer Tools. Use at least one of the listed subtopics (Console output and filtering), include one normal input and one edge case, and write two sentences explaining why the observed result makes sense.
task_acceptance_criteria: The program uses the lesson concept accurately and has readable names.
The learner states the expected result and checks the actual result.
At least one edge case, failure path, or environment assumption is addressed.
hints: Reduce the program to the smallest example that still shows the concept.
Trace values and control flow from the first statement to the output.
Use the linked official reference when behavior is unclear.

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a snippet without understanding its input and output.
common_mistakes.why: A memorized example can appear to work while hiding assumptions about input values or runtime.
common_mistakes.fix: Explain the expected output first, run the smallest example, and test one boundary case.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming browser APIs are part of core JavaScript.
common_mistakes.why: ECMAScript does not define the browser DOM or Node.js filesystem APIs.
common_mistakes.fix: Identify the host environment and consult its official API reference.

common_mistakes.why: Several simultaneous edits make the cause of a behavior difficult to isolate.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one variable or line, reproduce the result, and record what changed.

summary: JavaScript Developer Tools describes a specific behavior or tool that should be tested with an observable example.
